no-circular.comment: A cycle whose edges survive type erasure makes initialisation order load-order dependent.

backend-recursion-circular.comment: A backend's exonode and its instance renderer naming each other. Inert: no ring member reads a ring binding at module evaluation. See BACKEND_RECURSION.

type-only-circular.comment: A cycle that exists only in types. Erased at build; reported, not fatal.

not-to-unresolvable.comment: An import that does not resolve is a broken build waiting to happen. EXCEPT a Vite virtual module: `virtual:app-sloc` is produced by the plugin at packages/benchmarks/vite.config.ts:31 and exists only inside a Vite build, so a crawler that reads the filesystem cannot resolve it and never will. The exemption is that ONE specifier and not the `virtual:` scheme, so a second virtual module has to be added here deliberately. `@cnstra/exodra` is the other one: it peers on @exodra/core 0.3.0, so it reaches npm only after this repo publishes, and until then the todo example aliases it to the cnstra source; drop it here once the example installs the published package.

no-undeclared-dep.comment: Imported but NOT in this package.json. It works in the monorepo (hoisted node_modules) and breaks for whoever installs the published package.

core-names-only-context.comment: @exodra/core names ONE Exodra package, @exodra/context, and no other — not even a types-only one. THE ONE NAME IT MAY SPEAK is the context chain, which core CALLS in exo-base-node-pack.ts; context-is-zero-dep below is the other half of that statement, and it is what keeps the pair acyclic. THE WORD "RENDERER-AGNOSTIC" STOOD HERE AND WAS FALSE TWICE: this rule reads the IMPORT GRAPH, and a module knows the DOM without importing anything. src/list/ called insertBefore under it for months (now @exodra/list-reconcile), and events/ typed a handler Event and Element, which made @exodra/term cast a fabricated object through a type it could not satisfy. What core actually is: the SCHEMA VOCABULARY, plus the HTML facts every backend re-derives otherwise — void elements, raw-text elements, escaping, and which attributes have a property form. Those are markup knowledge and they stay; @exodra/term ignores the last one by name (exoTermWriterForPort.ts). The gate for what this one cannot see is packages/core/src/tests/coreNamesNoDom.test.ts.

bench-harness-is-bench-only.comment: @exodra/bench-harness is a private, never-published measuring instrument — the interleaved runner, the clock-grain probe and the null-pair resolution report the package benches share. core-names-only-context, computed-names-only-core and context-is-zero-dep each exempt it by name, which would be a hole in each if anything but a bench could name it. This rule is what closes that: the ONLY files allowed to import it are the ones under a `bench/` directory, so a shipped module borrowing the harness fails here rather than sliding through an exemption written for something else.

context-is-zero-dep.comment: @exodra/context is a frame of three fields, a token of one, and the walk that reads a chain. @exodra/core imports it, so an import in the other direction would close a cycle through the package every backend links first. It names no Exodra package and no DOM name either, which is what lets @exodra/term and the server renderer link the whole of it. THE ONE EXEMPTION is @exodra/bench-harness, which src/bench/ names and nothing published does: it is private, it is excluded from this package's emit by tsconfig.json, and bench-harness-is-bench-only above is what holds it to bench files.

computed-names-only-core.comment: @exodra/computed is the DECLARATIVE half of a machine — fields, derivations, transitions, the pending word. It sits on top of the imperative builder that stays in @exodra/core, so the direction is computed -> core and never back; core-names-only-context above is the other half of the same statement. It names no backend either: a field is a bit and a derivation is a function, and the one thing written at the end goes through connector.set, which every backend answers.

list-reconcile-is-zero-dep.comment: @exodra/list-reconcile holds the passes that CALL DOM APIs — insertBefore, removeChild — which is exactly why they are not in @exodra/core. It names no Exodra package in return, so the direction is dom -> reconcile -> nothing and a backend with no document links none of it.

backends-do-not-know-the-reconciler.comment: THE OTHER DIRECTION, and the one that was never checked. `list-reconcile-is-zero-dep` above proves reconcile -> nothing; this proves backend -> nothing-reconcile. Reconciling is a layer over two doors a backend already has — `build` to make a row and the child list to place one — so a backend that imported it would be a backend with one list strategy welded in, and a second strategy could no longer be a second FUNCTION. Tests reach it freely — `options.exclude` drops them from the crawl — and they are where the composition a user would write is driven. The older comment above says "the direction is dom -> reconcile"; no runtime file in any backend has named it for some time, and this rule is what keeps that true. BOTH SPELLINGS, per the header: the alias resolves to packages/list-reconcile/src, and with no alias the import lands on the node_modules symlink.

renderers-do-not-know-each-other.comment: The live (dom) and snapshot (string) renderers deliberately share only core primitives — never each other.

renderers-do-not-know-each-other-reverse.comment: The other direction of the same rule.

hydration-is-a-leaf.comment: Nothing outside @exodra/dom hydrate/ may import from it except the package barrel — one value import from an always-retained module welds hydration into every client-only bundle.

runtime-does-not-import-build-tooling.comment: Compilers, plugins and scaffolding run at BUILD time. A runtime package importing one would ship it to the browser.

error-registry-does-not-ship.comment: Nothing a package publishes may import from scripts/ — the error-code registry there holds exactly the explanations a production build strips.

no-deprecated-core.comment: Deprecated Node core modules will be removed.
